items.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023
items.q: he played for me a vinyl, you know it was a compilation of recordings from the 40s from Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker. That was the very first thing I ever heard about.

ctx.x: what’s going on in your head when you’re — like I was watching one of the many recordings or videos of your “Funky Cha-Cha.” And you’re playing these very intense bebop lines and so forth and I’m wondering what’s going on up there?

You know let’s rewind sixty years and I’m going to tell you — I started in my village, because I grew up in the village in the countryside of the island. I started playing traditional Cuban music with local bands, that was the first thing. And then I went to school later on to get classical training and I spent three years in that school, strictly classical. In that school, that was funny, we weren’t allowed to play, talk or listen to anything but classical music. It was like a military kind of thing. And then…
You just answered one of the questions I had written down, so thank you. Does the fact that you play piano impact your trumpet improvising?
